state.name: Convert video to MP4 (H.264)
state.description: Picked codec and quality with fast-start for streaming.

category.instructions: Which category best describes this hub command? Judge from state.cmd (the raw command text); state.tag and state.cli are hints only. This is a casual-user tool that replaces online converters, compressors, PDF tools, and media utilities with offline shell commands — prefer a media/file category over a developer one when both fit. Renders into the Details Category row, the Safety Category row, and the tag badge.

criteria.video_tools: Everyday video jobs: change format or codec, shrink file size or quality, cut or trim clips, join clips, resize resolution, pull out the audio track, grab thumbnails or make GIFs; reads video and writes video, audio, or image files
criteria.audio_tools: Everyday audio jobs: change format (mp3, wav, flac, ogg), shrink bitrate, cut or trim, join tracks, normalize or change volume; reads audio (or video, when extracting) and writes audio files
criteria.image_tools: Still-image jobs: change format (jpg, png, webp, avif), resize dimensions, shrink quality or file size, make thumbnails; reads images and writes images
criteria.pdf_tools: PDF jobs: join PDFs, split out pages, shrink PDF size, turn PDF pages into images, build a PDF from images or documents; reads or writes .pdf files
criteria.document_tools: Non-PDF office and text conversion (docx, txt, md, csv and similar) via converters such as pandoc or LibreOffice; writes documents that are not PDFs
criteria.archive_tools: Pack files into zip, 7z, or tar archives, unpack them, or list their contents
criteria.file_organizers: Tidy files without converting anything: batch rename, move or sort into folders, find duplicates; operates on file names and folder trees
criteria.download_tools: Save a remote file to a local copy (curl or similar downloading into a file); the output is a local file, not terminal text
criteria.developer_tools: Project script workflows (bun run, npm run, build, test, lint, dev server); effects depend on the named script — legacy hub entries
criteria.network_io: Sends HTTP requests and prints the response as terminal text (curl GET fetch or POST deploy hook); writes no local file — legacy hub entries
criteria.other: Does not fit any category above

operation.instructions: What single operation does the command perform? Pick the closest match from the observable command text. Tiebreaks: shrinking size or quality beats format change (compress over convert); saving to a local file beats printing (download over fetch); building a PDF beats converting images (pdf_create over image ops). Renders into the Safety Operation row with an estimated pill.

criteria.video_convert_format: Changes video container or codec (for example mkv to mp4, H.265 to H.264); the format change is the point, not shrinking
criteria.video_compress: Shrinks a video file or lowers its quality (crf, preset, bitrate reduction); size reduction is the point
criteria.video_trim: Cuts a time range out of a video (start time plus duration); outputs a shorter clip
criteria.video_merge: Joins two or more clips into one (concat); the inputs are multiple videos
criteria.video_resize: Changes frame dimensions or resolution (scale); the picture size changes while the container stays
criteria.video_extract_audio: Pulls the audio track out of a video into an audio-only file
criteria.video_to_gif: Makes an animated GIF from a video clip; the output is a .gif
criteria.frame_extract: Grabs a single still frame from a video (ffmpeg with -vframes 1); the output is a poster image
criteria.audio_convert_format: Changes audio container or codec (wav to mp3, flac to ogg); the format change is the point
criteria.audio_compress: Lowers audio bitrate or file size; size reduction is the point
criteria.audio_trim: Cuts a time range out of audio; outputs a shorter track
criteria.audio_merge: Joins two or more audio tracks into one (concat)
criteria.audio_normalize: Adjusts loudness or volume (loudnorm, volume filter); the level change is the point
criteria.image_convert_format: Changes still-image format (jpg, png, webp, avif); the format change is the point
criteria.image_resize: Changes image dimensions or makes thumbnails (scale, resize); the picture size changes
criteria.image_compress: Lowers image quality or file size; size reduction is the point
criteria.pdf_merge: Joins multiple PDFs into one document
criteria.pdf_split: Extracts pages or page ranges out of a PDF into new files
criteria.pdf_compress: Shrinks a PDF file (downsample, recompress); size reduction is the point
criteria.pdf_to_images: Renders PDF pages out as image files (png, jpg)
criteria.pdf_create: Builds a PDF from images or documents; the output is a .pdf
criteria.doc_convert: Converts office or text documents to another non-PDF format (docx, txt, md, csv); the output is not a PDF
criteria.archive_create: Packs files or folders into a zip, 7z, or tar archive; the output is an archive
criteria.archive_extract: Unpacks an archive or lists its contents; the input is an archive
criteria.file_batch_rename: Renames many files by pattern in place; names change while locations do not
criteria.file_organize_move: Moves or sorts files into folders, or reports duplicates; locations change while content does not
criteria.file_download: Saves a remote URL to a local file (curl with -o or -O, download to a path); the output is a local copy
criteria.file_info_read: Only inspects files (probe, info, list, metadata); prints facts and writes nothing
criteria.security_audit: Runs npm audit over installed packages, with or without fix
criteria.container_build: Builds a container image from the working directory (docker build)
criteria.container_run: Starts a container from an image (docker run)
criteria.history_read: Only reads commit history (git log); changes nothing
criteria.branch_delete: Deletes local branches already merged into main (git branch -d, possibly via xargs)
criteria.network_post: Sends an HTTP POST that can trigger side effects server-side (curl with -X POST); prints the response
criteria.network_get: Sends an HTTP GET and prints the response to terminal text; saves no file (a download to a file is file_download instead)
criteria.script_run: Runs a project script (bun run or npm run); effects depend on that script
criteria.other_general: A general task matching none of the operations above; falls back to the hub category

produces.instructions: What does running the command with example values produce? Look for output files, destinations, or response patterns in state.cmd. Renders into the Safety Produces row with an estimated pill.

criteria.video_file: Writes an encoded video container (.mp4, .mkv, .mov) or a .gif
criteria.image_file: Writes still images (converted, resized, thumbnails, or frames extracted from video or PDF)
criteria.pdf_file: Writes a PDF document (.pdf): merged, split, compressed, or newly built
criteria.document_file: Writes a non-PDF document (docx, txt, md, csv)
criteria.downloaded_file: Saves a remote URL to a local file copy
criteria.modified_file: Writes or modifies a file in place
criteria.stdout_response_only: GET prints the response without writing files
criteria.readonly_terminal_output: Prints history, findings, or file facts; writes nothing (git log without delete, audit without fix, probe or info commands)
criteria.unknown: No output file, destination, or response pattern detected in the command text

risk.instructions: How destructive is this command if run with example values? Return the severity level. Casual converter and compressor commands are usually Low unless they auto-confirm overwrites. Renders into the Safety How destructive row as a Low/Medium/High pill plus reasons.
criteria: Low: read-only, or writes only new output files; deletes nothing and confirms nothing automatically
Medium: auto-confirms overwrites (-y, --force), triggers remote side effects (POST), builds or starts containers, or rewrites dependencies (audit fix)
High: deletes data (rm -rf, git branch -d, xargs with -d)

mutates_files.instructions: Does the command write or change files, images, containers, lockfiles, or remote state? Renders into the Safety Mutates files Yes/No row.

criteria.true: Writes or changes media, PDFs, documents, archives, containers, lockfiles, renames or moves files, saves downloads, or changes remote state (output refs, -o, docker build/run, -vframes, movflags, crf, POST, audit fix, branch -d)
criteria.false: Read-only; writes nothing (history inspection, plain GET, audit without fix, probe or info commands)

deletes_data.instructions: Does the command delete files or branches? Renders into the Safety Deletes files Yes/No row.

criteria.true: Deletes branches or files matched by the command (rm, git branch -d, xargs with -d, delete)

overwrites_files.instructions: Could existing files be replaced without asking? Renders into the Safety Overwrites files Yes/No row.

criteria.true: Possible: auto-confirm flags (-y, --force), media, PDF, or archive output extensions, output refs, -o, shell redirect, POST, or audit fix
criteria.false: No overwrite detected in the command text
